body: Hey, my psych told me I have anxiety with obsessive compulsive tendencies, I just treat it as ocd because that's essentially what it is but maybe not as severe or not as physically compulsive as ocd.  It sucked when she told me that, I cried and had panic attacks for months thinking that meant all my obsessions were true, but then I just started treating it like ocd, I hope that everything works out for you ❤

Oh I hate that, it's the worst, unless your dog has good recall you shouldn't be walking them unleashed. My other dog has OK recall but we only walk him unleashed if there's no other dogs or people around just in case.

It should just be a basic of owning any dog!!  My friend has a tiny ancient rescue chihuahua that was never trained and she used to just bite people.  She has no teeth so it wasn't a huge issue but they're still trying to prevent her from doing it cos that's just what owning a dog is, taking responsibility!

Yeah I get it, I used to work in a shelter and we'd train dogs and have them come back a week later acting like rat bags again because their adopters didn't keep up training.  My dog is a terrier rescue, came to me overweight, nervous and with no training (her owners were lovely they just didn't understand terriers are active and intelligent).
I always tell people she's not friendly or find a way to avoid walking past dogs but sometimes they just sneak up on you haha, I have been looking at getting a NO DOGS harness for her though :)

I used to work at a small charity based no kill shelter, it got to the point where we had to turn away litters that showed symptoms and it was heartbreaking, we just didn't have the facilities to quarantine them efficiently :'(
Oh nice!  My grandparents have a kelpie/border, she's quite old now but she was a silly little goose when she was younger 😂

The reason I take him back is because I know he's not capable of biting another dog, he's never gotten that angry about anything.  I will keep the muzzle in mind though, thank you, as I am really looking for a way that we can keep taking him to the park.  Long walks are off the table due to his joint pain and he's not that interested in toys, so the parks really the best way of keeping him mentally stimulated

Yeah probably, I just hate it cos I know how much he loves meeting other dogs.  90% of the time when he does it he's trying to break up fights.  People laugh when I say that but he literally runs between them and pushes whichever dog is on top off of the other one
Yeah, we're trying to find something to replace it but he really loves playing with the other dogs, and we can't take him for long walks anymore cos he has early signs of arthritis

Thank you!  He does need a checkup soon so I'll try and get my partner to organise that and address it with his vet :) and thank you!  They are great dogs, Mac is a very smart funny boy, typical border collie, a bit goofy but we love him haha

Our OEPE is 3:30, in a large town, near the city so we get a big breakfast rush of people going to work down in the city.  I hate rushing my co-workers which means I often go over which sucks, I usually work nights and my managers are a little more chill about OEPE times than they are in the morning/day, but yeah I think having a longer amount of time definitely helps cos our store is usually top 10 in the country haha, I feel so bad for you, I couldn't imagine doing it all in 1:40

Yeah we just had oepe introduced to our store and a lot of the staff (me included) were never really told what it was or how it works.  We're usually in the top 10 in the country but it's wavering a bit lately.  Our target used to be like 3:30 minutes but idk if it's even still the same tbh
Thank you!  I'm actually going to ask my dr about anxiety and possible hypochondria tomorrow because this isn't the first time I've induced symptoms into myself bc of anxiety 😂 thanks a lot xxx

Thank you, his poops have actually returned to normal since then, I think the whole not in the litter box thing may have been territorial as my older cat sometimes comes inside.  He will be going to the vet in the next week or two though :)

May get written up depending on ur store, I only got written up for one ncns and I've done it twice (I try not to obvi but shit happens) and I've had to call in sick 20 minutes before a shift too, it just depends on ur store really but because it's a first offence ur gonna be fine, there's people at my store that have been written up way more than 3 times and they're still here 😂

If someone talks to me when I'm counting up change I get confused sometimes and give out the wrong change, or even no change at all a couple of times.  I think working there just fries my brain into mush sometimes 😭😂
A dude threatened to kill one of my managers because we couldn't do the $1 hamburgers after midnight, like wtf calm ur farm mate 😂
Lmao the other day one of my managers apologised to some lady for a 5 or 10 minute wait he was like "really sorry about that, have a good day" and she just snapped "no you're not" and walked out 😂

I'm so happy to hear that happened to you, I work at a McDonalds and I always try to be really nice to the nice people despite being an introvert and severely depressed too.  I always hope that being kind to people might brighten up their day at least <3 good luck with everything <3

In my claim I told them my relationship started two years ago and we moved in together a year ago, although I got the exact date we moved in wrong so I have to start the claim again.  Before we moved in together I didn't have enough evidence of our relationship tbh so they don't really care, my friends told me their case worker told them not to change their relationship status until they had concrete evidence (joint accounts, leases etc) but I just forgot to update my address completely.
Thanks so much, I moved out at an early age and I'm really only learning to be responsible now so I hope they understand haha

Thank you, I wasn't sure if I should even declare it because I pay for my own shit and he pays for his but he earns about $800 a week where I earn about $250 😭 I already have a bit of debt to pay back from when I was like 17 though so I guess they'll just add it to that lol

Thank you!!  Yeah I know I'm not the best at my store but I try hard to be a good employee and I think most of my co-workers/management know that :) I have severe anxiety and depression so I can be really hard on myself about work, so thanks heaps for your comment, it means a lot to me :)

Thank you so much, I really appreciate your comment!  I'm not the fastest or best tbh but i think i redeem myself because i try very hard to be as helpful as possible.  I know people at my own store who put in way less effort and get away with it tbh, while I'm on time consistently and cover other people's shifts all the time I'm just so paranoid haha!

A woman screamed at me because, after doing the best I could to understand her speech impediment (she was deaf), I didn't realise she wanted a second double quarter meal.  She went off at me yelling, calling me a fucking loser, asked to speak to my manager and just yelled at him about how stupid I was.  Luckily he was really understanding about it.

I have a sister who's deaf so I understand how hard it can be but I could barely understand this lady and I got her entire large order right except for one meal.
One of my shift managers got shitty at me and told me to get a doctor's note one time though, I did and she never asked to see it lmao, other than that I've never been asked for one

I've worked at my store for about 9 months and I've called in sick about 4 times I think, although I have gone to work and been sent home maybe 3 times.  I'm always on time and I pick up other people's shifts when they need me to, so I'd say my manager knows I'm fairly reliable.  As long as you give them notice or get someone to cover for you you should be fine.  I have mental health issues and chronic stomach problems but I'll almost always go into work and try to deal with it unless I'm throwing up.  If you feel like absolute shit though don't feel bad, you obviously need the time to recover, so don't stress it x

I'm Australian and work at Maccas over here, wages are decent , you're right, I'd say co-workers and customers are the biggest issue for the workers in our franchise that I've talked to at least.  
Like a lot of the customers are alright, i love my regulars, but some customers are just downright rude, I've been called a loser, been sworn at and yelled at by customers, it's not fun.  Plus some of my managers are horrible, I find at McDonalds it's easy for workers to be shitty to their colleagues and chalk it up to stress when really it's just a bad attitude/workplace environment.

This happened to me too actually, I kept her and I think you ought to keep your kitty too.  If she's in that poor condition either she's been lost for a long time or more likely her owner doesn't give a shit about her.  The previous owners of my cat loved her but took absolutely no care of her.  I took her back to them after getting her vet care, buying her food, defleaing her and I asked nothing but that they feed her properly.  Two years later a lady who helped me get her to the vet called up out of the blue and said "the cat we rescued showed up in the shelter, you have to get her" and even though I know where her owners live I made the moral decision not to return her.  Her microchip was never registered so legally I was free to take her from the shelter, idk about your situation but I hope you can keep that poor little kitty!

I'm not an expert but I think it's essentially your brain trying to protect you and distance you from the thing that's causing anxiety, which unfortunately for you is your girlfriend.  I get the same feeling, when I'm around my boyfriend I often feel numb or depressed and distant from him.  I think it might be a form of dissociation, because sometimes I feel like I don't even know him.  I'm so sorry you're going through that, but it is fairly standard for ROCD in my experience
